title: Zesty Silky Ethiopian Oats Dabo
description: A citrusy and nostalgic Ethiopian dish featuring oat milk and long-fermentation-dough, made gluten-free-friendly in the traditional dabo form.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine teff flour, yeast, salt, and sugar.
Gradually add oat milk to the dry ingredients and mix until a smooth batter forms.
Knead the batter for 10 minutes until it becomes elastic and sticky.
Place the batter in a greased bowl, cover it with a damp cloth, and let it ferment in a warm place for 24 hours.
Preheat a non-stick skillet or dabo pan over medium heat.
Add olive oil to the pan and swirl it around to coat the bottom.
Pour the fermented batter into the pan and cook for 5 minutes or until the bottom is golden brown.
Loosen the edges of the dabo with a spatula and flip it over.
Cook for an additional 5 minutes or until the other side is also golden brown.
Remove the dabo from the pan and brush it with lemon juice and sprinkle with orange zest.
